title: SOLA: Optimizing SLO Attainment for Large Language Model Serving with State-Aware Scheduling
technique: iteration-level state-aware scheduling: per-iteration constrained optimisation over request order and per-iteration workload, driven by per-request and system-wide TTFT/TPOT-to-SLO ratios, on vLLM

optimized_metrics.evidence: we propose a fine-grained scheduling framework to maximize the SLO attainment for LLM serving.
optimized_metrics.locator: §1 (Introduction), txt line ~240 of raw text / abstract

optimized_metrics.evidence: The goal of scheduling in LLM serving is to maximize the request processing rate of the system under TTFT and TPOT constraints.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: the agreement between service providers and users determines SLOs (e.g., TTFT ≤ 0.5s, TPOT ≤ 0.1s) as the latency constraints

optimized_metrics.evidence: The goal of scheduling in LLM serving is to maximize the request processing rate of the system under TTFT and TPOT constraints.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: the agreement between service providers and users determines SLOs (e.g., TTFT ≤ 0.5s, TPOT ≤ 0.1s) as the latency constraints; TPOT measures the average latency during the decode phase

optimized_metrics.evidence: The goal of scheduling in LLM serving is to maximize the request processing rate of the system under TTFT and TPOT constraints.

headline_claim.text: Given SLO constraints, the evaluation shows that SOLA enhances the SLO attainment from 45.5% to 99.4%, and serves 1.04-1.27x more requests than the state-of-the-art systems on average.

reported_metrics.where: normalized goodput at 90% and 99% attainment (Fig 8/9, §6.5 SLO sensitivity)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For each request, TTFT measures the latency of waiting and the prefill phase, while TPOT measures the average latency during the decode phase.
Considering that TPOT measures the average latency per output token (except for the first token)
metric_definitions.notes: average over decode tokens excluding first

metric_definitions.definition_quote: attainment (i.e., the percentage of requests within the SLOs)
metric_definitions.notes: per-request: must satisfy both TTFT and TPOT SLOs (box in TTFT-TPOT plane)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we define p_i^{TTFT/TPOT} = max_r(t_{i,r}^{TTFT/TPOT})/T^{TTFT/TPOT}. The real-time attainment of TTFT/TPOT SLO is 100% if p_i^{TTFT/TPOT} <= 1.
metric_definitions.notes: internal scheduler state uses MAX over running requests of latency/SLO ratio, not a percentile

metric_definitions.definition_quote: compare the goodput (i.e., the maximum input request rate) under 90% and 99% SLO attainment.
metric_definitions.notes: goodput = max request rate (req/s) sustaining 90% or 99% attainment; not SLO-meeting tokens/s

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TTFT and TPOT measure the request-level latency perceived by users, while throughput and goodput measure the system-level performance.

slo_spec: SLO = multiple of single-request latency: 10x (tight) / 15x (loose) for 7B-14B models; 5x / 10x for 70B-72B (batch size shrinks with larger models). Specific numbers in Table 3 (e.g. 0.8/0.2s, 1.2/0.3s TTFT/TPOT). Goodput at 90% and 99% attainment.
load_regime: request-rate sweep (Poisson-style input request rate), ShareGPT and LongBench sampled
tradeoff_acknowledged: Core framing: trade-off between TTFT and TPOT (prefill-first helps TTFT, hurts TPOT; decode-first reverse) and among requests; no loss of a third metric claimed.
extractor_notes: Optimizes attainment of joint TTFT+TPOT SLO (mean-style TPOT per request; no tail percentile of latency). Goodput here is request-rate at 90/99% attainment. PDF read from MLSys proceedings; layout text two-column so line refs are to raw pdftotext.
load_class_quote: generate request arrival times using Poisson ... increasing input request rates and compare the goodput (i.e., the maximum input request rate) under 90% and 99% SLO attainment (§6.1)
